failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Query at hop 2: 'Was Geoffrey Chaucer the first poet to be buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey, and was John Fecknam the last abbot of Westminster Abbey?' - This is formulated as a natural-language yes/no question rather than entity names or key phrases, which is a shape the retriever cannot use well.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 retrieved 'Geoffrey Chaucer' and 'John Feckenham' articles confirming all claim elements. Hop 2 query asked 'Was Geoffrey Chaucer the first poet to be buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey, and was John Fecknam the last abbot of Westminster Abbey?' and retrieved the same 'Geoffrey Chaucer' article again. Hop 3 query 'Westminster Abbey, Geoffrey Chaucer, John Fecknam' also retrieved the same 'Geoffrey Chaucer' and 'John Feckenham' articles again. All three hops fetched essentially the same documents.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 solver reasoning extensively analyzes passages about 'John Denham (poet)', 'John Hutchison (sculptor)', 'Dean of Westminster', and 'Abbot of Westminster' - none of which are relevant to verifying the claim. The solver states 'Passages [5] and [4] discuss the Abbot of Westminster and its succession to the Dean of Westminster, but none of the provided passages explicitly state who the last abbot was' when passage [2] from hop 1 already confirmed John Fecknam was the last abbot.

failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 2, the solver states 'However, the provided passages do not contain information to verify the claim about John Fecknam being the last abbot of Westminster Abbey' in summary_2. But passage [2] from hop 1 (which was part of the context) explicitly states 'John Feckenham...was an English churchman, the last abbot of Westminster.' The solver had access to this information but claimed it was absent.
